```text
# PR #3453: Patch: promotions stop timing out: the patch source test loads a bounded set of snapshots, and each ci-scope case answers for one file

Closes #3418

Both tests that stuck the promotions no longer time out. The change is limited to two test files. One part needs a person: the two cases this change moves to the daily run will not run anywhere until someone adds one path to `super.yml`. Details are under "Needs a person" below.

## What changed

**`apps/web/src/patches/source.test.ts`** (#3443, `web (unit 4/8)`, "Test timed out in 30000ms")
- **Per pull request:** the case "R388 the real source reads crates/cards/patches/…" now loads 10 snapshots instead of all 134 (64 MB):
  - the brief's first six versions;
  - `v0.2.0b`, whose 317 cards it still counts;
  - the newest 3 (`NEWEST_SNAPSHOTS`), since promotions only append (R646).

  It still checks the order of `patches.json`, the shipped prefix and the `core-065` prefix of the index. Its 30 s limit stays, and its work no longer grows with each `patches ship`.
- **Daily** (`daily(...)` from `src/test/daily.ts`), each with a `// daily:` comment saying why:
  - the full sweep over every snapshot;
  - "R388 the index lists, for every card, exactly the versions…".

  Each gets 180 s (`EVERY_SNAPSHOT_MS`), as the similar walks in `diff.test.ts` and `placeholders.test.tsx` have. Per pull request, the bounded case above holds the loading of snapshot files. The Rust test `crates/tools/src/patches.rs` `r388_derives_each_patchs_card_by_card_changes_and_the_per_card_index_from_the_snapshots_alone` reads every snapshot and holds each patch's changes and `index.json`. It is not ignored, and any change under `crates/cards/` runs its group.

**`apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`** (#3415, `web (unit 7/8)`, "Test timed out in 5000ms")
- The db case ran the script 57 times inside one test. It is now one case per file, which is the file's own rule ("One case per file … so a case never nears vitest's time limit").
- The other cases built the same way were heavier, so they are split too: web (74 runs), e2e (63), Rust groups (49), promote-production (42), clippy (14) and infra (17). Every assertion is unchanged; only the grouping changed.

## Needs a person

- **Add the path to `super.yml`.** The daily `web-extra` step runs only a fixed list of paths (`src/audio/ src/fx/ src/cards/art/convention.test.ts src/net/promote-*.test.ts src/tutorial/scripts/`). Add `src/patches/source.test.ts` to it, or the two daily cases above never run. The bot cannot edit `.github/`.
- **An older gap of the same kind.** The `daily(...)` cases already in `src/cards/versionLooks6.test.tsx` and `src/cards/defaultLooks.test.tsx` are not on that list either, so they never run today. Adding those paths fixes it.
- **Close this issue** once this merges, so `patches-ship.yml` ships again from the newer main and supersedes #3443.

## How I tested it

To stand in for a busy runner, I pinned vitest to one CPU core with two busy loops (`yes`) on the same core. I ran this on the newest promotion branch, `origin/patches/ship-c7e599e43b` (140 snapshots), in a scratch worktree I removed afterwards.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Result | 2 failed, 145 passed | 333 passed, 2 skipped (the daily cases) |
| `source.test.ts` sweep | "Test timed out in 30000ms" | bounded case 2.9 s of 30 s |
| `source.test.ts` index case | "Test timed out in 5000ms" | daily |
| `ci-scope` web / e2e / db cases | 4.67 s, 4.02 s, 3.77 s of 5 s (passed, barely) | slowest case 0.69 s |

- **Uncontended on main:**
  - The sweep took 20.2 s and now 0.99 s.
  - The slowest `ci-scope` case took 1.73 s and now 0.22 s.
  - The `ci-scope` file took 14.6 s before and 12.4 s after.
- **The daily cases** with `JACKIOH_DAILY=1` on the promotion branch: 8 passed. The sweep took 18.0 s, and the index case run alone (`-t "R388 the index lists"`) took 19.3 s. That is why it gets its own limit: the default 5 s would fail it.
- **Other checks**, all passing:
  - `pnpm exec eslint` on both files.
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`.
  - `cargo jackioh spec check`: "1849 rulings … ok".
  - `cargo fmt --check`.
  - The harness's web command `vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …`: 2 files, 333 passed, 2 skipped.
  - `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: "classify: Internal", so no patch fragment is needed.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **The newest 3 snapshots, not every version a promotion ships.** The newest promotion ships six. The test cannot tell which versions a promotion added without git, and the Rust test already reads every snapshot on each pull request. Making the newest-N count large would bring the growth back.
- **Splitting every list-driven `ci-scope` case, not only the db one.** Under load the web case came closest to the limit (4.67 s). Fixing only the db case would leave the next promotion to time out on the web one.
- **One case per file, rather than batching files into one script run or raising the timeout.** Batching would change the interface of `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, which `ci.yml` uses. The maintainer ruled out a timeout-only fix, and the file already states the one-case-per-file rule.

## Worth a second look

- **The new test titles.** The renamed cases put the file in the title (for example "runs web for %s, which its job reads"). The path-scan cases at the end of the file also start with "runs web for …", but their titles end in "…, which <file> names", so they stay distinct.
- **Other walks over every snapshot.** `diff.test.ts` and `placeholders.test.tsx` still walk every snapshot per pull request, at 180 s each. They grow the same way, but with about six times their current headroom (27 s of 180 s in CI). I left them alone.

Closes #3418.

- Error: `Test timed out in 5000ms`. It was the only failure: 1 of 1196.
- **The cause.** That test makes git commits and runs `scripts/ci-scope.sh` three times for each of about 25 files, all under vitest's default 5-second limit, on a runner spawning 63 workers.

- **Why it grows.** The test loads every snapshot through Vite's JSON import (`import.meta.glob` in `source.ts`). The history is 134 snapshots totalling 64 MB, and each shipped version adds about another 0.5 MB. So the test slows with every patch, and a promotion run, which loads the most snapshots of all, is where it runs out of time.
- **Fix direction.** Per pull request, read a bounded set of snapshots:
  - the first six;
  - `v0.2.0b`, which the test counts;
  - the newest few, since promotions only append (R646);
